subject: Post-call: BrightLane POC — success metrics & evaluation playbook
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chang <emily@brightlane.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 22, 2026 at 15:08 PDT
Subject: Post-call: BrightLane POC — proposed success metrics & next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier. Appreciate you walking us through the BrightLane onboarding flow and the main friction points. As promised, I’m sending a concise recap + a proposed evaluation playbook for the POC so we can align on ownership and timelines.

Summary of objective:
- Validate Redwood can meet BrightLane’s production requirements for the recommendation microservice used in the publisher flow (real-time content suggestions).

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 150 ms on the production-like test harness (95th percentile across user-shaped traffic).
- Throughput: sustain 500 QPS with 100 token average per request while keeping latency SLOs.
- Cost: model-run cost <= $0.0018 per 1k tokens (target unit economics threshold).
- Quality: recommendation relevance NDCG@10 >= 0.42 against your internal test set, and manual review pass rate >= 88% on a 200-sample set.
- Reliability: 99.9% availability during the two-week validation window, with graceful fallback to the baseline model on degradation.

POC timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): alignment on datasets, access, and test harness.
- Week 1: infra provisioning and model onboarding; Redwood prepares a dedicated test instance.
- Week 2: run baseline & competitor trials, gather telemetry.
- Week 3: metric-driven tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization experiments).
- Week 4: run final validation & handoff; produce results and runbook.

Ownership:
- BrightLane: provide evaluation data, pass/fail criteria, and a technical contact to finalize test harness (Emily + Solutions Team).
- Redwood: provisioning, model variants, tuning knobs, telemetry dashboards, and final evaluation report (Alex + Sergio).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Emily — confirm the data export cadence and preferred sample for the manual review (200 items).
2) Emily — share credentials or temporary S3 access to the sanitized test set by Mon Apr 27.
3) Laura — I'll need a canary plan for routing and an SLO escape hatch for production-like tests; can you draft a short runbook?
4) Sergio — can you own the model/infra rubric and confirm resource estimates by EOD Fri?

Attachments: BrightLane_POC_Success_Metrics_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — draft thresholds and measurement plan.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Emily Chang <emily@brightlane.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 23, 2026 at 09:14 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLane POC — proposed success metrics & next steps

Thanks Alex — this is super helpful and aligned with what the product team wants to validate. Quick responses inline: 

- Data export: we can provide a sanitized S3 bucket with event-level logs + ground truth labels by Apr 27. Will send the IAM stub today.
- Manual review: 200 items works. We’ll add an internal rubric so reviewers score relevance/false-positive rate.
- Latency target: 150 ms p95 is aggressive but within expectations if you can show consistent results under load.

A few asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood include an embedding-based reranker variant in the trial? We want to compare response quality vs. the dense-only model.
2) Please provide a short questionnaire for security/compliance (SOC2 scope) so our InfoSec can sign off on the temporary test access.

I’ll loop in our Solutions Team and schedule the data drop. Looking forward to seeing the dashboard outputs.

—Emily Chang
Head of Product Integrations, BrightLane
emily@brightlane.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chang <emily@brightlane.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 24, 2026 at 11:02 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLane POC — proposed success metrics & next steps

Emily / Alex — I can own the model/infra rubric. A few technical notes and confirmations: 

- We will provision a dedicated test pool (n1-standard equivalent + 1x A10G) to mirror your production footprint. Initial config will be: 2 workers, batching window 8–12ms, token limit 256.
- Variant plan: dense-only baseline + embedding-reranker variant + a quantized 4-bit candidate for cost runs. We’ll measure token/sec, p95 latency, and token-level cost for each variant.
- Measurement details: we’ll run a 6-hour continuous soak at 500 QPS and then 2 x 30-min ramp tests at peak to capture tail behavior.
- Telemetry: we will provide per-request traces, p50/p95/p99 latency, token counts, and cost breakdown per route. Dashboards will live in Redwood Console and we’ll share a view-only link.

Questions for BrightLane:
- Can you confirm the average prompt length (tokens) for the recommendation request and whether there’s any per-request context (user history) we should cache?
- Any specific privacy constraints for the test data beyond sanitization?

I’ve attached a technical checklist and the initial resource estimate.

Attachments: BrightLane_POC_Technical_Checklist.pdf (stub)

—Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chang <emily@brightlane.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 27, 2026 at 08:21 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLane POC — proposed success metrics & next steps

Quick update: 
- Emily — received the IAM stub and S3 path, thanks. Laura and I will review the rubric and the manual-review criteria once you share.
- Sergio — appreciate the soak plan; can you post the resource estimate into the shared Drive folder (link below) so BrightLane can confirm budget?

Proposed kickoff: Tue Apr 28 at 10:00 PT for a 30-min alignment (data ingress, test harness endpoint, dashboard access). If that works I’ll send calendar invites. 

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_BrightLane-POC

Thanks — aiming to keep the timeline tight so BrightLane can validate within May.

Alex

From: Emily Chang <emily@brightlane.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, May 03, 2026 at 11:20 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLane POC — proposed success metrics & next steps

Alex / Sergio — kickoff confirmed for Tue Apr 28 10:00 PT (calendar accepted). A couple of final confirmations before we start: 

- We accept the proposed success thresholds for the initial run. If Reed (our Director of Data Science) has follow-ups, we’ll surface them during the 30-min kickoff.
- For the embedding-reranker variant: please include an evaluation script so we can reproduce NDCG numbers locally.
- Our InfoSec reviewed the questionnaire and requested a short SOC2 evidence bundle; I’ll upload that to the Drive by EOD Mon.

Looking forward to the tests and thanks for the clear plan.

Best,
Emily
